about.title: Downey Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: When a product fails and injures someone in Downey, California law is on the consumer's side. Unlike most injury cases, product liability often runs on strict liability — you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. Defects can be in the design, in the manufacturing, or in a missing warning. These cases can involve everyone from the manufacturer to the distributor to the retailer, and they frequently require engineering experts and preservation of the product itself. LawProactive connects injured Downey consumers, at no cost, with an independent product liability attorney. You pay nothing unless the case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why these cases move fast on evidence

items.title: Keep the product
items.desc: Do not repair, discard or return the item that hurt you. The product itself is often the most important piece of evidence, and preserving it can make or break the claim.

items.title: Strict liability helps you
items.desc: In many California product cases you don't have to prove negligence — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. That's a meaningful advantage.

items.title: Multiple parties may be responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers can all share liability. An attorney can identify every responsible party and every applicable source of recovery.

items.question: What counts as a defective product?
items.answer: California recognizes three kinds of defects: a design defect (the product is unsafe as designed), a manufacturing defect (something went wrong in making it), and a warning defect (it lacked adequate safety warnings or instructions). Any of the three can support a claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the company was careless?
items.answer: Often not. Product liability in California frequently proceeds under strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that the manufacturer acted negligently.

items.question: What should I do right now?
items.answer: Keep the product and its packaging, save receipts and photos, get medical care, and avoid contact with the manufacturer's representatives until you've spoken with an attorney.
